speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic; I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues. To better understand your condition, can you describe exactly how the pain started and what activities were you doing at the time?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Oligoarticular type) or Reactive Arthritis secondary to an occult infection, given the unilateral swelling in a toddler without trauma and a reported family history of similar issues. I would like to proceed with further examination and testing to confirm the etiology. REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, Antinuclear Antibody (ANA), and Uric Acid. REQUEST TEST: Right Knee Ultrasound to assess for joint effusion and synovitis.
